text:
For a renter, I’d start with the **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W solar-panel kit**. It’s a portable battery-and-panel setup: put the panel on the balcony when it’s sunny, bring the power station indoors, and plug your devices into the station. The listing gives it a **288 Wh** battery and says it can handle phones, a laptop, a router, or a fan—but **not a refrigerator**. [See the kit and price](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2-100w-solar-kit).

If you want longer runtimes, look at a roughly **1,000 Wh station with a 200 W panel**; a good solar day may add around 500–750 Wh, but shade, clouds, and balcony direction can cut that substantially. Solar on a balcony is a recharge option, not a substitute for plugging in at home. [TrueWatt’s balcony-solar guide](https://www.gettruewatt.com/guides/balcony-solar)

Before setting up, check your lease/building rules and make sure the panel can’t fall or blow away. This kind of kit is different from **plug-in balcony solar**: it charges a separate battery and does not connect to your apartment’s wiring.
